text: Master data management: the discipline of getting one organization to agree on who its customers, products, vendors, and employees actually are. This course spends twenty-five lessons on exactly that problem.

Master data is the core set of entities multiple systems reuse — customers, products, vendors, employees, locations. Three traits set it apart: it's reused across many processes, not generated once; it changes slowly, unlike a transaction log; and it's relatively low in volume but very high in value — get one customer record wrong, and every order tied to it inherits the mistake.

Picture one real customer, seen three different ways: the CRM has 'Robert Chen,' the billing system has 'Bob Chen' with an updated address, the shipping system has 'R. Chen' with an address from two years ago. Each system is correct about something. None of them, alone, answers 'who is this customer, right now?'

This shows up the moment it matters most: a merger duplicating half a product catalog, a marketing campaign mailing the same person three times, an opt-out that doesn't stick because it only applied in one system. Master data problems are invisible until they're suddenly very visible.
Next: how master data is different from reference data and transactional data — three categories that get confused constantly, and a clean way to tell them apart.
